Subject: Jordan Tech — kickoff prep: model shortlist + token plan

Team —

Quick context: Jordan Tech (contact: Peter Jordan / Amelia Roos) are ready to move from evaluation to an implementation kickoff. They build a business intelligence assistant that ingests customer contracts and provides clause summarization + question answering across multi-doc case files. Key asks from the sales call:
- Runtime latency SLO: 300–500ms 95p for interactive flows
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~15 (but can burst to ~30 for heavy reporting windows)
- Average doc chunk size: ~2,500–3,200 tokens; retrieval will stitch 3–5 chunks for context
- Compliance: SOC2 plus customer-managed VPC preferred (private deployment option needed)

Please draft a practical model shortlist and a realistic monthly token estimate they can use for procurement and Dedicated sizing. Include: recommended context length, expected input vs output token split, latency expectation per model, and rough GPU footprint (dedicated vs shared).

Can we have a first-pass by EOD today? I attached the mutual action plan we shared (jordantech_mutual_action_plan_v1.pdf).

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Jordan Tech — kickoff prep: model shortlist + token plan

Hi all — first pass below. I focused on models we can serve efficiently on Redwood Dedicated and with good instruction-following for RAG. Notes on assumptions: avg input chunk 3k tokens, typical prompt + system ~200 tokens, average generated answer ~220 tokens. Monthly active users estimate pending — I used the numbers from the sales deck (1,500 MAU with 2 average queries/day).

Shortlist (ordered by recommendation):
1) mistral-instruct-7b (int8)
   - Context: 16k (recommended for multi-chunk stitching)
   - Expected latency: 120–220ms/token; single-request median 220ms for 1–4k context; 95p within 400ms on optimized A100 pool
   - Cost footprint: fits on 1x A100-80GB with quantized weights (dedicated slot); good throughput for concurrency 15–30 with autoscaling

2) redwood-inference-13b (q4_k_mixed)
   - Context: 16k
   - Expected latency: 180–320ms median; 95p ~500ms under 15 concurrent sessions (recommend dedicated pool of 2 GPUs for headroom)

3) llama-3-70b (quantized) — fallback / high-quality option
   - Context: 32k optional (if they need very long single-document context)
   - Expected latency: 350–700ms; requires multi-GPU sharded dedicated nodes (4x H100/A100 depending on quantization), higher cost but better on complex synthesis tasks

Token-volume estimate (based on sales-provided usage):
- Assumptions: 1,500 MAU x 2 queries/day x 22 workdays/month = 66k interactions/month
- Per interaction: 3,000 input tokens * 3 chunks = 9,000 input tokens; output 220 tokens average
- Monthly input tokens ≈ 594M tokens; monthly output tokens ≈ 14.5M tokens; total ~608.5M tokens/month

Operational notes / tuning levers:
- Use prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts in interactive sessions to reduce token processing for the system prompt and instruction templates
- Chunking strategy: 2.5–3k chunk size with 3 chunks (tunable) — reduces context tokens while keeping recall high
- Canary plan: start with mistral-instruct-7b (int8) in a small dedicated pool; measure latency/cost for 2 weeks; switch traffic to redwood-13b for high-quality paths if needed

I'll drop an xlsx with numbers and a short estimation sheet (redwood_model_shortlist_estimates.xlsx). Happy to refine if sales updates MAU or concurrency.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Thanks Rachel / Dev — useful breakdown. A few clarifying items from our side before we lock capacity: 

1) Our average document uploaded per customer is ~18 pages; after preprocessing chunking it comes out to roughly 2.8k tokens per chunk. We typically stitch up to 4 chunks for QA flows (so closer to 11k input tokens for some queries).
2) Peak concurrency: 15 typical, but we see spikes to ~40 for end-of-quarter reporting (short windows, 10–15 minutes).
3) Compliance: SOC2 is required; we do prefer VPC/private deployment.

Also — cost sensitivity is material. We'd prefer starting on a smaller model (mistral-instruct-7b) and then move to redwood-13b only for customers where quality delta is visible.

Attaching a small sample of typical payloads to help you run perf tests (jordantech_sample_payloads.json). Can we also confirm a proposed kickoff/canary date? We're aiming for Feb 18–19 for initial rollout testing.

Best,
Peter Jordan
Director of Data Products | Jordan Tech

   - Secondary / quality path: redwood-inference-13b (q4_k_mixed), 16k context — used for customers with high-quality needs

2) Token sizing update (owner: Monica)

3) Deployment & compliance (owner: Stephanie)

4) Canary & timeline (owner: Rachel)

   - Action: Jordan Tech to confirm preferred timezone window for the 2-hour ramp test (we recommend 10:00–12:00 PT).
